Tuesday 23 June 2026 at 00:00 UTC. Norway and Senegal on the card. On the Senegal side, the engine's number sits +12.0pp clear of the market — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards this far out from kickoff.

On Elo, Senegal comes in 30 points ahead — Norway at 1760, Senegal at 1790. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Senegal to win at 39%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Senegal on the win side reads 39%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 48%, the draw at 25%, and Senegal to win at 27%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Senegal side — 27% on the market, 39% on the engine, a +12.0pp gap.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Senegal, that haircut lands the model at 32%; the market is at 27%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.8pp. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 27 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the Senegal side still clears the Pick threshold.

copy.summary: A +12.0pp gap across model and market on the Senegal side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Senegal at 39%; Polymarket sits at 27%.
copy.title: Norway v Senegal · the model leans Senegal
